SECTION 1
* The article shares letters from young people responding to politician Sajid Javid, who defended millennials being blamed for not being able to buy houses just because they spend money on small luxuries like avocados or holidays.

* The first writer, a 24-year-old, complains that older people criticize him for enjoying small pleasures like meals out or vacations, insisting he should save every penny for a house instead.

* He argues that buying a home is nearly impossible anyway because house prices keep rising, fewer homes are available, and banks are less willing to give out loans (mortgages) than before.

* He feels frustrated that many young people will likely have to rent forever, giving their money to landlords who then turn around and accuse them of being financially irresponsible.

* The second writer points out that young workers are actually paid less by law—the "national living wage" doesn't apply to under-25s, so they can earn as little as £5.60–£7.05 per hour for the same work, and they're more likely to have unstable zero-hours contracts.
